key_insight: The paper introduces Agent-Guided Concept Discovery, a concept-based learning framework that learns interpretable biochemical concepts directly from REIMS data without requiring concept labels.
engineering_relevance: This could improve intraoperative surgical margin assessment by making deep learning models more explainable, more adaptable to noisy operating-room spectra, and easier to trust clinically.
method: Learns latent concepts from raw REIMS spectra instead of relying on predefined concept annotations.
Uses a reasoning agent to refine semantic descriptions and reweight concepts by diagnostic relevance.
Grounds discovered concepts with a biochemical knowledge graph to align them with known metabolic relationships.
evidence_signal: Across Skin and Breast Cancer datasets, the model improves balanced accuracy and sensitivity over the baseline, and in a representative intraoperative case it produces fewer false positives.
watch_item: Clinical deployment may still be limited by how robustly the discovered concepts transfer across hospitals, instruments, and real-time surgical noise conditions.
paper_title: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery: Toward Interpretable Surgical Margin Assessment
